title: Parachute onboarding: multi-file weights admission, deterministic conversion, and pinline validation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an end-to-end 'parachute' onboarding flow for new open-source LLMs focused on robust multi-file weights intake, deterministic conversion to the runtime format, artifact provenance, and a pinline validation harness that publishes a performance profile to the catalog. This ticket covers the orchestration glue, policy checks, and the smoke/benchmark validators needed to safely recommend a canonical pin. Key goals: 1) Accept heterogeneous uploads (sharded checkpoints, safetensors, merges) and normalize a stable canonical artifact; 2) Run deterministic conversion with reproducible checksums and a signed manifest; 3) Execute automated smoke validations: KV-cache correctness, generation coherence on canonical prompts, token-level regression checks, micro-latency and memory profiling on representative hardware; 4) Produce a pin recommendation with a published performance profile (latency P50/P95, memory, quantization compatibility notes) and provenance metadata for the catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Intake: pipeline accepts multi-file uploads (tar/s3-manifest) and emits a canonical artifact with SHA256 and signed manifest
Conversion: deterministic runtime blob generated reproducibly on CI and matches checksum across two different builder instances
Smoke validations: KV-cache correctness test and 20 canonical prompts pass fuzzy-output thresholds compared to reference outputs
Performance profile: P50/P95 latency, peak memory, and tokens/sec measured on the target dedicated instance and attached to the model profile
Pin publication: a versioned pin with metadata (commit, converter-version, quantization-compatibility, license) is written to the catalog and surfaced in console
Rollout safety: automated fallback policy exists if subsequent runtime smoke fails for the pinned version
tasks: Design intake manifest schema and signing fields (include license, source_url, checksum list)
Extend artifact-gateway to support tarball and s3-manifest ingestion with backpressure handling
Implement deterministic converter runner with reproducible seeds and environment snapshots
Add a lightweight smoke harness: kv-cache tests, prompt regression suite, and microbench wrapper
Wire telemetry: detailed per-run latency/memory traces, conversion logs, and publish to model-catalog topic
Create pin recommendation heuristics (latency vs quality vs memory) and UI payload for Console
Add automated security/license scan step and block pins for incompatible licenses by policy
risks_and_notes: Multi-file ingestion increases attack surface; enforce signed manifests and restrict compute for untrusted assets
Determinism requires pinned builder images and deterministic dependency sets — coordination with infra is needed (see ENG-142859)
Quality regressions are subtle; fuzzy thresholds must be conservative initially to avoid incorrect pins
Quantization compatibility checks can be slow; we will stage them as async checks with a preliminary pin that flags quantization status
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with infra and security. Agreed on signed manifest approach and a minimal manifest spec (license, file-list, sha256, source_url). Action: Maya to draft spec in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ARTIFACTS/Parachute-Manifest
2025-02-20: Prototype converter runner implemented in CI; reproducibility verified across two containers on x86-gpu. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2763
2025-02-24: Smoke harness v0 added with KV-cache correctness test. Observed a 3% output divergence on long-context LLaMA-style checkpoint — investigation assigned to Diego
2025-02-28: Security scan integrated using license-checker and yara rules. A community checkpoint flagged for embedded PII in sample tokens; blocked from auto-pinning and escalated to compliance
2025-03-01: Bench harness added to dedicated staging pool to capture P50/P95 and peak-oom. Initial runs show memory within expected envelope for 8k sequences on target instance
next_steps: Finish deterministic converter edge cases (partitioned linear layers, custom operators)
Stabilize fuzzy-output thresholds and expand canonical prompt set to cover instruction-style and long-context scenarios
Add UI surface for pin metadata and a manual override flow for model reviewers
Schedule a security review with compliance (requested 2025-03-04)
Pilot with two community models and publish the first two pins to staging catalog by 2025-03-12
